subject: Priv deploy — MPA sequencing, escrow evidence triage
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@remedohealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: samir.patel@remedohealth.com
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood private deploy — initial redlines and evidence ask

Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and security reviewed the MSA and the order form for the private (on-prem) deployment and pushed back on a few areas we need to triage before procurement can sign:

- License scope: we need to confirm whether operator-run snapshots (for backup/witnessing) are covered under the standard license or require a separate Exhibit.
- Audit / evidence: our compliance team asks for an escrow-like evidence pathway — options include (a) sealed snapshot deposit with third-party custodian, (b) witnessed snapshot with a Redwood engineer present, or (c) scheduled remote forensic session. They want to see a short pros/cons list and sample language.
- Operator access & access window: we want a defined access window for troubleshooting; please confirm minimum notice and access control (just-in-time, RBAC).
- SLA carveouts: for on-prem we need a fallback SLA and an explicit outage escalation for stateful operator actions.

Attached are our annotated MSA and the Order Form. Can you map these asks to a mutual action plan and suggest a timeline? Procurement would like a clean legal pass within three weeks if possible.

Also: Samir is on copy from legal — he may propose alternate wording. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute review this week.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Director, Procurement — Remedo Health
E: e.ortiz@remedohealth.com
T: +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: Redlined_MSA_Remedo_v1.docx (MS Word, redline), OrderForm_Remedo_Draft.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — initial redlines and evidence ask

Elena — thanks for the clear list and the redlines. I reviewed with product and legal briefly and here is a proposed sequencing so we can keep procurement moving:

1) Narrow license boundary (2 business days): Confirm whether operator-run snapshots are within the granted runtime license or need an Exhibit. Marissa will draft a short Exhibit option and a minimal-purpose clause (snapshot for failover + compliance).

2) Evidence pathway options (4 business days): We will draft three sample clauses for the escrow-like ask you outlined (sealed snapshot with custodian, witnessed snapshot, remote forensic session). Include estimated security controls and costs.

3) Operator access & notice (2 business days): Laura to confirm RBAC/JIT controls and propose a 4-hour emergency window + 48-hour scheduled access for non-emergency work.

4) Order form/SLA carveouts (3 business days): Aditya will update order form language and pricing impact for any Exhibit or witnessed-support line items.

Proposed next steps: I’ll assemble a short MPA (mutual action plan) PDF and share it by end-of-day. Can we target a joint legal review call Tuesday 2027-06-03 at 10:00 PDT? That gives us time to produce the sample clauses.

Internal owners: Marissa -> legal wording / Exhibit; Laura -> operational controls; Aditya -> commercial/order form.

If that looks good, I’ll send the MPA and a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
+1-650-555-0134

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: 2027-06-02T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — initial redlines and evidence ask

Folks — I pulled together preliminary legal notes after looking at Elena's redlines. High-level thoughts (will expand in the doc attached):

- License scope: prefer a narrow Exhibit that permits snapshot creation and transfer solely for remediation and compliance. Avoid granting any right to run the model beyond the contracted usage. Suggested phrasing: "Snapshot custody limited to forensic & disaster recovery; operator access requires documented MPA events."

- Escrow-like evidence: third-party sealed snapshot is easiest from a liability standpoint but increases cost and logistics. Witnessed snapshot (Redwood engineer on-site) has lower custodian risk but higher operational friction. Remote forensic session is lowest cost but weaker for some auditors — we should provide language for all three and mark tradeoffs.

- Audit window: propose a 30-day rolling window for audit requests and a 48-hour minimum notice for non-emergency operator console access. For emergency remediation, include a 4-hour response SLA to begin access, with detailed post-action reporting.

- Data handling & egress: include explicit confirmation that snapshots are encrypted at rest, keys remain with Remedo unless escrow route chosen, and any transfer to custodian must be mutually agreed.

I attached legal_notes_privdeploy.docx with suggested redline snippets and a proposed cost note for the three evidence options. If we aim for the 6/03 call Jasmine suggested, I can have the redlines and a brief speaking note ready.

– Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: legal_notes_privdeploy.docx
